findings.claim: The post-generation manifest claims a temp tree built from git-index tracked source refs and a PASS verdict for clean-checkout regeneration.
findings.failure_mode: The verifier uses git ls-files --cached only as a path allowlist, then copies bytes from the mutable working tree with shutil.copy2. It never asserts git diff --quiet / git diff --cached --quiet, records a HEAD/tree SHA, or reads blobs from HEAD/the index. A local tracked-file edit or missing tracked worktree file can be reproduced in the temp tree while a real clean checkout of the release commit would not contain the same bytes.
findings.required_repair: Build the temp tree from an immutable recorded commit using git archive/git worktree or read blobs from the index/HEAD; fail on dirty worktree, staged changes, or missing tracked files; record the commit/tree SHA and a full tracked-source manifest hash in the reproducibility report.

findings.claim: The manifest verdict PASS supports regeneration of the current release-critical post-generation reproducibility artifact set.
findings.failure_mode: The post-generation reproducibility manifest itself is not in tools/verify_oc133_reproducible_temp_tree.py COMPARE_REFS and is not one of the 11 compared rows. The verifier writes this report after comparison, and the Lean build certificate only records post_generation_reproducibility_manifest_ref as a path without a hash. A stale or locally edited manifest can therefore be shipped without any byte-for-byte regeneration check for this release-critical artifact.
findings.required_repair: Add a check mode or outer verifier that generates the post-generation manifest in a temp checkout, compares its SHA-256 to the current report before overwriting, and records the report hash in a non-cyclic outer attestation or split stable payload.
